chunks: And from him, from Isma'il, from Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Murhibi, from Abu al-Hasan the Second (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, saying: 'A man doubted during the circumambulation (Tawaf) and did not know whether he had circumambulated six times or seven.' He said: 'If it is in an obligatory [Tawaf], he must repeat it for every doubt he has; and if it is in a voluntary [Tawaf], he builds upon what is lesser.' And likewise, if his doubt is in what is less than six, then if it is in an obligatory Tawaf he repeats, and if it is in the voluntary [Tawaf] he builds upon the lesser. He narrated that.

key_terms.بَنَى عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ: He built upon the lesser (assumed the lower count)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for doubt in the number of circumambulations during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'building on certainty' (ibtina' ala al-ashbah) for voluntary acts, contrasting it with the stricter requirement of repetition (i'adah) for obligatory Tawaf to ensure validity. It reflects the Shia juristic methodology of distinguishing between the rigorous standards of fard (obligatory) rituals and the leniency applied to nafl (voluntary) worship, ensuring that minor doubts do not invalidate the spiritual effort. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for resolving ambiguity in ritual actions where the baseline is assumed to be incomplete until proven otherwise.
